recipes.name: Steakhouse Wheat Bread for the Bread Machine

steps.text: Place warm water, butter, honey, salt, coffee, cocoa, sugar, bread flour, whole wheat flour, and bread machine yeast in the pan of a bread machine in the order listed. Put on regular or basic cycle with light crust.

raw_recipe.headline: Steakhouse Wheat Bread for the Bread Machine
raw_recipe.description: Instant coffee, cocoa, and honey may seem like strange partners in a bread recipe until you actually try this one made like a favorite steakhouse version.
raw_recipe.name: Steakhouse Wheat Bread for the Bread Machine

recipeInstructions.text: Place warm water, butter, honey, salt, coffee, cocoa, sugar, bread flour, whole wheat flour, and bread machine yeast in the pan of a bread machine in the order listed. Put on regular or basic cycle with light crust.

review.reviewBody: I have a Zojirushi 2 lb loaf bread machine. I adjusted this recipe as follows: 1 1/4 cup water,1 1/2 tbls. butter/marg, 3/4 tsp salt, 2 cups bread flour, 1 1/4 cups whole wheat bran flour, 2 tsp. Red Star Active Dry Yeast. I eliminated the sugar, and left the honey, coffee and cocoa powder the same as original recipe. I also added 1 tsp. gluten flour. The bread came out perfect......it rose right up to the top of bread pan. I used basic bread/medium crust setting.

Used tea drinker's Zojirushi modification for my Zo, increasing the ingredients for a 2 lb. loaf and it worked perfectly, (used butter, not margarine). I monitored the kneading cycle to make sure the dough was not too wet and it was not. Perhaps that's because of the addition of the vital wheat gluten recommended by tea drinker. It was light, mildly crusty (would probably use the dark crust setting next time, instead of medium, as we like a crunchy crust) and not too sweet. I used SAF yeast 2 1/4 teaspoon. Went over very well: plain, sandwiches, etc. grace614

I made this bread .. and oh my goodness.. I LOVED it, and I will be making it again!

I did make 2 changes.. since I can not tolerate coffee, I left the coffee granules out.. and I also added brown sugar instead of white.

I have a Panasonic SD YD250 .. I set it on the Whole Wheat Bake Rapid, Medium loaf, 3 hour cycle.. and it was soooo good !

Perfecttttt!! My family absolutely LOVED this bread. Sooo addicting! I wouldn’t change anything about it. I baked this in my mother’s old Welbilt ABM3500 bread machine, basic cycle (option 1), 1 pound setting (this recipe is for a 1 lb bread -setting - I was originally confused since the recipe didn’t state that), color: light and it baked perfectly! This will definitely be a staple bread recipe for years to come. Also, bread yeast is rapid rise yeast/instant yeast. I personally used the Fleischmann’s bread machine yeast (1 1/4 tsp. as indicated above) and made sure the water I used was 110 degrees.

Perfect! Amazing! I did not have cocoa powder, so I used chocolate syrup and warmed it a bit (like the kind you use to make chocolate milk.) I did not have coffee granules, but I did have leftover coffee, so I used that instead. I used 1/4 c. of coffee and reduced the amount of water to 1/2 c. minus 1 Tbsp to account for the liquid in the chocolate syrup.

I wouldn’t change anything. I’m a novice bread machine user and this is the first bread I’ve made in it. It was easy to follow and it came out perfectly! I was hesitant to try it since there were some mixed reviews but from my limited research, I would say if it came out bad, then either the setting was wrong for the bread (make sure you use the white bread/basic setting even though it’s wheat bread technically, also I used light crust), the loaf size was wrong (I used 1.5 lb and it was perfect), or the ingredients were layered wrong. The recipe says to do liquid first then dry on top but your machine may call for the opposite so you need to read the manual. Also, the yeast cannot touch the liquid when you put it in. My machine manual said to put in the flour then dig a little well type of thing in the flour to sit the yeast in. 

The bread came out soft inside and nice crunchy outside crust. The flavor is really nice too. It’s the type of bread you want to keep eating, great accompaniment to dinner. :) I followed the recipe exactly with the same exact ingredients as listed and it was perfect. I will continue making this bread pretty often!

I don't have a bread machine, so I used my stand mixer. I proofed my yeast in 1/4 cup of water and 1 tbs brown sugar, then added the butter and 1/2 cup very strong coffee and the honey. I used 1 cup of whole wheat flour and 1 cup of AP and 2 tsp vital wheat gluten with the salt and cocoa powder. The dough was very soft so I kneaded in about 3/4 cup more flour to achieve a well kneaded dough. I allowed it to rise until doubled, about 45 minutes, formed my loaf and allowed to rise again about 45 minutes and baked at 375 for about 30 minutes in a well greased, glass loaf pan. I will make it again sometime when it isn't so humid to see how much of a difference that made. All in all it tastes good, toasts well and I had no complaints from my tasters. Thanks for sharing the recipe.

This was the second loaf I ever made in my bread machine (the first was the basic "Best Bread Machine Bread"), and I was a bit nervous to try something so complex so early, but I needn't have been. It was a complete success!!! Totally loved another reviewer's suggestion to top it with butter--amazing! Anyway, I have a 2.5-lb Panasonic bread machine with automatic yeast dispenser. Did 1.5 times the original recipe and set the machine to Bake, Whole Wheat, Medium Loaf (which is the smallest setting for the model). I followed Panasonic's instructions for adding the ingredients, not the recipe's, and used active dry yeast rather than bread machine yeast. Perfection.

Edit: Just tried a doubled-recipe batch on the large loaf setting (the second of the machine's three sizes), and it came out perfect too.
Used this bread to make French toast. Best we ever had. Used iron skillet, topped with confectioners sugar, maple syrup and strawberries!

LOVE this recipe!! So delicious- and wonderful hearty crust in the bread machine. I’ve made it as written several times, and last night- I tried a little variation: used cinnamon flavored coffee instead of water, and added slivered almonds into the ‘add-in’ stage of the machine. The house smelled divine!! The bread was true heaven! The choco-coffee-nut combo was exquisite. The color came out darker: I used Ghiridelli cocoa powder, dark honey, and cinnamon flavor coffee. Going to make it again tonight, trying Christopher Elbow cocoa, and Cameon’s Highlander Grog coffee, with oats and almonds. Great use of wheat flour recipe- and SO EASY!!

This was great bread! I made it according to the recipe, but began to worry because the dough did not rise like most do in my bread machine (I make bread several times a week). So I took it out after the first rise, and formed a loaf in a regular loaf pan, then let it rise in a warm spot for over an hour. Baked at 350 for about 30 minutes and it was perfect. This IS dense, but that was what I wanted! I could taste the coffee in it, though, it gave it a tiny bit of a bitter twang, so next time I will leave that out.
There needs to be more liquid in the recipe. Mine was just stirred flour. It never did make bread.
Made as directed in a Cuisinart compact bread machine set to light crust. We all loved it. I am making another loaf right now.

Good however 2 T of butter would have made a better loaf and an idiot below thought that 2 C of flower was 1 1 1/2# which is laughable. I have not tried scaling it up to a full loaf but if I do I'll post that version.
Wow, excellent! Tastes just like the Steak & Ale bread. Yummy!!

It was very goopy with 30 minutes left and I thought it was a failure. Was I wrong. It did cook up just fine. I would recommend increasing the recipe by 2. I did the light crust and while it was good….maybe medium would be better.
